name: providence-analytics
description: Providence is the 'All Seeing Eye' that measures effectivity and popularity of software. Release management will become highly efficient due to an accurate impact analysis of (breaking) changes
author: ing-bank

scripts.test:node: npm run test:node:unit && npm run test:node:e2e

dependencies.@babel/parser: Lazily imported by AstService (the `--fallback-to-babel` parser) and referenced from the emitted declarations, so optional
dependencies.@rollup/plugin-node-resolve: Dev-only: the suites mock the file system with mock-fs, which a native resolver cannot see, so test-helpers swaps it in through importResolver.setResolver
dependencies.@swc/core: Lazily imported by AstService for the `swc` ast type - every shipped analyzer uses `oxc`, the base Analyzer defaults to `babel` - and referenced from the emitted declarations, so optional
dependencies.oxc-parser: Pin it as long as the api is unstable, to prevent unpredictable behavior
dependencies.oxc-resolver: Resolves import specifiers from a directory (exporter.sync(dir, specifier)) with the ESM conditions and `module` field, at ~0.008ms/call versus ~1.7ms/call for a fresh @rollup/plugin-node-resolve instance; miniDevServer (src/program/utils/mini-dev-server.js) reuses it to resolve bare specifiers for the browser
dependencies.semver: Only needed for one check. Create internal util later

devDependencies.lit-element: Only the optional dashboard (providence dashboard) needs it in the browser; the dashboard is served by our own dev server (src/dashboard/server.js + miniDevServer) since we dropped @web/dev-server
